findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "book_service" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Use when the person has decided to buy a Polystate service — e.g. 'book the Wyoming LLC', 'start my Paraguay residency'. With a Polystate API key it starts a ch…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "get_tax_rates" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_residency_programs, check_licensed_agent · Private data: visa_check, book_service, tax_compare, get_visa_requirements, get_legal_changes, get_tax_treaties · Public sink: get_residency_programs, check_licensed_agent.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_residency_programs, check_licensed_agent · Private data: visa_check, book_service, tax_compare, get_visa_requirements, get_legal_changes, get_tax_treaties · Public sink: get_residency_programs, check_licensed_agent

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
